title: CopyCat vs Outmarket: insurance AI software compared
summary: Outmarket has bells and whistles most agencies don’t need. CopyCat focuses on crucial P&C workflows: commercial and personal lines proposals, comparisons, policy checking.
body_markdown:
The short version


- CopyCat turns carrier documents into an editable, agency-branded proposal in about 90 seconds on average.
- The most advanced proposal editor in the category, and the easiest to use: click in like a Word doc, or ask the AI to make the edit. Revision history behind it.
- Every demo and onboarding session is led by a founder, and the founders stay your direct line: 5 to 15 minute email response, 1 to 6 hour average turnaround on feature requests.
- Seat-based, month-to-month pricing: no contract, cancel anytime, a discount for an annual agreement, and new features included. Outmarket charges based on pages processed, and its terms are ambiguous: different agencies, different terms.
- No document cap on comparisons and unlimited file storage. Outmarket caps how many documents go into a comparison and limits storage.
- Low friction by design. No feature bloat, no training program, no admin to configure. Producers are making proposals on day one.
- Outmarket has a lot of bells and whistles that, in our experience, about 90% of agencies don’t need. CopyCat is super focused on the core P&C workflows, commercial and personal lines proposal generation, quote comparisons, renewal summaries, policy checking, and contract review, and offers more features inside each of them.
- Known for state-of-the-art proposal software, CopyCat also offers one of the best quote and renewal comparisons in the category and a wide variety of agency marketing material: one-pagers, email summaries, and market summaries.


Producers ask us how CopyCat compares to[Outmarket](https://outmarket.ai/) . Both are AI platforms built for insurance brokers. CopyCat is not the smaller product. It is the more focused one. CopyCat is known for state-of-the-art proposal software, and it also offers one of the best quote comparison and renewal comparison workflows in the category, plus a wide variety of marketing material for the agency: one-page summaries, email summaries, and market summaries in the agency's brand. It is low friction, faster per proposal, molded to each agency's template and workflow, supported by the founders, and sold on terms you can explain in one sentence. Here is the side-by-side, with the things we can speak to on our own product and what Outmarket has told us or published about theirs.


> “I love that I'm not locked into a contract.”
> *A CopyCat customer who came over from Outmarket*


That line comes up a lot. Agencies that switch tell us the contract is the first thing they notice, and the proposal speed is the second.

## What the table actually means


Outmarket is a broad broker AI suite, and proposal generation is one module inside it. CopyCat is built around the proposal itself and the workflows that feed it. The proposal editor is where that shows most. It is the most advanced editor in the category and also the easiest to use: click into the proposal like a Word doc, fix a value, and type, or ask the AI to make the edit and it carries the change out end to end inside the document, with revision history behind it. The template is yours, pixel for pixel. During onboarding CopyCat runs a branding call with your team to shape the proposal for the highest chance of conversion, and the final decisions stay yours. Every demo and onboarding session is led by a founder, and the same people you meet on that call are the ones you email when you want something changed. There is no handoff to a support queue after the sale.


That workflow fit is deliberate. The initial CopyCat product was built in person with brokers, sitting beside them and watching how work actually moved from quote intake through review and client presentation. Both founders took the commercial broker exam to understand the full broker lifecycle. CopyCat molds around how an agency works instead of asking the agency to reorganize itself around the software.


## Focused, not smaller


Outmarket has more bells and whistles. CopyCat does all of the core work too, and goes deeper on it. Outmarket’s breadth comes with a cost: every extra module is another screen to learn, another setting to configure, and another reason a busy producer goes back to the old way. CopyCat is super focused on the workflows that move the needle for a P&C brokerage, and it builds each one all the way through:


- [Proposal generation](https://www.runcopycat.com/insurance-proposal-software) , where CopyCat started and where it is strongest. The line we hear most often after a demo: “This is the best proposal generation app ever made.”
- [Quote comparisons](https://www.runcopycat.com/insurance-quote-comparison-software) across competing carrier options, with every value cited to the source page.
- [Renewal summaries](https://www.runcopycat.com/commercial-renewal-comparison-software) that show what changed between the expiring policy and the new one.
- Multiple proposal types from the same account: full client reports, one-page comparisons, and market summaries.
- Email summaries: send a summary of the proposal or the one-pager by email, along with the proposal itself.
- Policy checking that compares the bound policy against what was quoted, to assess E&O exposure before the client finds the gap.
- Contract review that reads a client's insurance requirements against their coverage.


Each of those is built the whole way through, molded to how the agency already works, and supported by the founders. Upload the carrier documents, get the proposal, edit it, send it. No feature bloat to wade through, no training program to schedule, no admin to babysit. Compare as many quotes as the account has, store every file, and never watch a page counter.


## The product you buy keeps getting better


CopyCat is not a proposal module that stands still after the contract is signed. The same platform now supports commercial lines, personal lines, employee benefits, and LTC/STC workflows. New features come directly from the problems customers bring us, and they are included instead of being turned into a new module and a new bill. Pricing is per seat and month-to-month: no contract, cancel anytime, no exit fees, with a discount for an annual agreement. Outmarket charges based on pages processed, and its terms are ambiguous: different agencies, different terms. Check the current contract for details.


The operating promise matters just as much as the feature list. The average email response time is 5 to 15 minutes, and a feature request turns around in 1 to 6 hours on average. Your team gets a person, a resolution, and a product that is more capable a few months after purchase than it was on day one. That combination makes CopyCat the straightforward choice for a brokerage that wants software molded to how it already works.


CopyCat is fully web-based, requires nothing to install, and never uses customer documents to train AI. If an output does not look great, reach out and the team will work on it with you.


## Try it on a real account


The fastest way to see the difference is to put your own renewal in front of CopyCat.[Bring a recent account](https://www.runcopycat.com/#contact) with the supplementals, carrier quotes, and the whole packet, and we'll run it live on the call. If it isn't obvious in the first five minutes, we'll tell you straight. And if Outmarket is the better fit for your agency, we'll tell you that too.

## CopyCat vs Outmarket FAQ


### What is the difference between CopyCat and Outmarket?


Outmarket is a broad AI suite for insurance brokers with more bells and whistles. CopyCat is tailored to the core commercial and personal lines P&C workflows and goes deeper in each: quote comparisons, renewal summaries, multiple proposal types (client reports, one-page comparisons, market summaries), policy checking for E&O exposure, and contract review. Each comes with a built-in document editor like Microsoft Word, an AI editing assistant, revision history, the brokerage's exact template, and founder-led onboarding. There is no document cap on comparisons, storage is unlimited, and pricing is per seat, not per page processed.


### How fast is CopyCat support?


The average email response time is 5 to 15 minutes. Feature requests turn around in 1 to 6 hours on average. Outmarket does not publish comparable figures.


### Can I edit a CopyCat proposal after it is generated?


Yes, and it is the easiest part of the product. Click into the proposal like a Word doc, fix a value, and type, or ask the AI to make the edit and it carries the change out for you. Revision history sits behind both. The template stays exactly the brokerage's own brand, colors, and sections.


### Does CopyCat require a long-term contract?


No. CopyCat is seat-based and month-to-month: no contract, cancel anytime, with a discount for an annual agreement. There are no exit fees and no charges per page processed. Outmarket terms are ambiguous: different agencies, different terms, and pricing based on pages processed. Check the current contract for details.


### Does CopyCat limit how many documents I can compare or store?


No. There is no document cap on comparisons and file storage is unlimited. Outmarket caps the number of documents in a comparison and limits storage.


### Who onboards a new CopyCat agency?


The founders do. CopyCat was built in person with brokers, and both founders took the commercial broker exam. The same people who onboard an agency are the ones it emails to request features or changes.
